messages:
marta: Heads up — noticed several GPU workloads that should land on gpu-warm are getting scheduled onto cpu-pool after yesterday's node drain. Looks like something in tolerations/affinity chain broke.
kevin: Seen that in the live dashboard. CA scaled up prod-gpu but warm pool stayed empty; pods fell back to cpu nodes. infra-bot logs show scale-up reason 'pods didn't fit'.
infra-bot: Cluster Autoscaler: scaleUp group 'prod-gpu' desiredSize 4 -> 6 (reason: pods didn't fit). https://console.example/internal/ca/events/17655
sophie: Quick question — are those pods using preferred nodeAffinity for pool: gpu-warm or required? If it's only preferred, scheduler may pick prod instead of waiting.
raj: FYI most model-serving pods have tolerations like: [{key: "gpu-only", effect: "NoSchedule"}] but our logging/metrics DaemonSets don't tolerate gpu-warm taint. When warm nodes drained the daemonsets couldn't run -> kubelet marked conditions and evictions cascaded.
marta: That fits what I saw. Warm nodes are tainted gpu-warm=true:NoSchedule and infra DaemonSets not tolerating it caused them to be unschedulable, so CA/eviction logic pushed user pods elsewhere.
kevin: Short-term fix: add toleration to logging/metrics daemonsets so infra pods can run on warm nodes. Medium-term: consider switching warm pool taint to PreferNoSchedule to avoid blocking infra DS.
sophie: Note on PreferNoSchedule — CA + scheduler interactions can still cause unexpected behavior. Also recommend adding an explicit nodeAffinity preference for gpu-warm to model-serving so they strongly prefer warm without preventing prod placement. Example snippet: 
```yaml
affinity:
  nodeAffinity:
    preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    - weight: 100
      preference:
        matchExpressions:
        - key: pool
          operator: In
          values:
          - gpu-warm
```
marta: Another angle: CA scaleDownDelay is 20m now which kept warm nodes longer than we want — cost impact visible. Reducing to 10m helps but increases risk of flapping during bursty workloads.
raj: Cost note: warm gpux nodes run ~0.8$/hr each; two idles ~38$/day. If tolerations let infra DS land, we can safely allow shorter warm windows and save money.
kevin: Action items I propose: 1) add tolerations to infra daemonsets (logging/metrics), 2) change gpu-warm taint from NoSchedule -> PreferNoSchedule in warm pool rollout, 3) add required/preferred nodeAffinity for model-serving pods, 4) reduce CA scaleDownDelay to 10m in canary region and observe.
marta: I'll open a PR for daemonset tolerations and schedule a CA config canary. Tagging @kevin for review. :thumbsup:
kevin: SGTM. Also add a test that simulates node drain + spot preempt to ensure pods don't fall back to CPU unexpectedly.
infra-bot: Pinned: PR #3421 created by marta — "infra: add tolerations to logging/metrics daemonsets". CI link: https://ci.example/job/3421
